newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 31.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi says the Freedom Alliance sabotages parliamentary works "with a scientific technique to lose time" but speaker of the Lower House says "it is pure opposition" (all).

* Left-wing Pds party leader Massimo D'Alema and right-wing opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi met again in a relaxed climate (all). But National Alliance leader Gianfranco Fini in an interview says the opposition should make "no presents" to D'Alema and warns that there will be a "frontal fight" over the 1997 budget (Corriere della Sera, Repubblica). The budget is due to go to the Lower House for discussion today.
* Three pundits named by the speaker of the Lower House in a report say bribes and corruption are still alive in Italy, only methods are more sophisticated (all).
* The government may decide to refund the "Eurotax", which Italians will be called to pay at the end of the year directly on their revenues or as an additional tax on luxury goods in 1999 (all).

* The government is discussing ways to recapitalize heavily indebted state holding company Iri. Prime minister Prodi says the best remedy remains the privatisation of telecom holding Stet. According to a Treasury statement, the sale of Stet will take place in any case by 1997 (all).

* Stock exchange watchdog Consob is reported to have asked ailing hi-tech group Olivetti for further explanations on the sale of its stake in British firm Acorn and its factoring operations (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
